tasks.short: Monitor donor health, safety and comfort during and after collection

steps.what: Monitor blood or plasma donors during and after procedures and respond to discomfort or deterioration

tasks.design: Keep donor monitoring and comfort support with the phlebotomist. Protocols in {DOCS} support escalation without replacing direct observation or staffed response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Donor deterioration may first appear in subtle physical or verbal signs.
tasks.enabler_now: Documentation tools do not establish a substitute for direct donor monitoring.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising early distress and responding promptly.
tasks.human_edge: Attentive observation, reassurance and timely intervention.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring coverage and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Retaining direct donor monitoring is an E1 judgement; the digest's scribe capabilities do not demonstrate monitoring automation.

assumptions: Boundary is direct monitoring and support during and after collection, excluding separate records and collection equipment runtime.
Phlebotomist directly observes responses in retained s1; no free distress score or structured adverse-event flag is assumed.
No new technology or workflow means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which donor changes require immediate clinical escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross0 and net0. Direct donor monitoring remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain fluid or tissue collection procedures to patients

steps.what: Explain collection procedures, answer questions and check the patient's understanding and readiness

tasks.design: Retain the explanation and understanding check with the phlebotomist, using approved {DOCS} material where useful. A leaflet or automated script is not assumed to remove questions, reassurance or consent-related communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients need explanations adapted to anxiety, language and the actual procedure.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference materials can support a conversation without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising misunderstanding or reluctance and responding appropriately.
tasks.altitude: No change to explanation time or patient communication responsibility.

reach.task: Address a collection concern beyond routine explanation

evidence.claim: Retaining patient-specific procedure explanation is an E1 design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is direct procedure explanation, excluding separate appointment instructions and actual collection.
Patient questions and understanding are elicited during retained s1; no structured ready-to-proceed flag or automated consent is assumed.
No new system means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Patient communication needs and local procedure information
research_questions: Which explanations require an interpreter or clinician?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, gross0 and net0. Explanation and understanding checks remain intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train medical personnel in phlebotomy and laboratory techniques

steps.what: Prepare the session from current procedures and the trainee's learning needs
Demonstrate techniques, supervise practice and assess safe performance

tasks.design: Use reusable approved session plans from {LMS} and current procedures in {DOCS}. Retain practical demonstration, supervised technique and competence assessment with the phlebotomist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated session preparation can duplicate established procedural content.
tasks.enabler_now: Native learning templates can organise current material without generating medical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Judging technique and correcting unsafe movements during practice.
tasks.human_edge: Specific feedback based on observed performance.
tasks.altitude: A little less preparation; practical teaching and assessment time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Assessment consistency and procedure version control

evidence.claim: Native session templates can reduce repeated preparation; this is an E1 task assumption, not a scribe-study result.

assumptions: Boundary includes trainer preparation and practical teaching, excluding trainee attendance time and organisation-wide protocol authorship.

Phlebotomist captures trainee identifier, learning objective, procedure version and practice requirements in s1's nine retained hours, including reading needs and checking the final plan. Missing requirements are resolved manually there.
Test native templates first. Two incremental trainer hours per 100 baseline hours cover plan freshness and links to approved procedures.
unknowns: Current learning system and recurring preparation effort
research_questions: Does a reusable plan reduce preparation after trainee-specific adaptation?

already_counted.description: Learning-needs capture, plan adaptation and procedure checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94; gross6 less2 upkeep gives4 net. Unusual trainees may need complete preparation and yield minus2; practical teaching retains85.

tasks.short: Determine donor suitability from interview, vital signs and history

steps.what: Interview the donor, obtain vital signs and clarify current medical history
Organise checked interview, vital-sign and history information for suitability review
Assess donor suitability against current criteria and refer uncertain or out-of-scope findings

tasks.design: Configure an information view in the {OTHER} donor record system using checked interview and measurement entries. The phlebotomist retains interview, measurement and suitability assessment against current criteria in {DOCS}, referring uncertainty to the authorised clinician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitability preparation can repeat copying between interview, measurement and history records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native donor record forms can organise captured information without deciding eligibility.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete histories, medical significance and the limits of the worker's authority.
tasks.human_edge: Clarifying sensitive answers and recognising uncertainty requiring clinical review.
tasks.altitude: Less information assembly; no expansion of eligibility authority.

reach.learn: Referral criteria and limits of screening authority

evidence.claim: Native organisation of donor screening information is an E1 design assumption; scribe capabilities do not establish automated donor eligibility.

assumptions: Boundary includes interview, vital signs, information preparation and suitability assessment within authorised scope; later collection and clinician decisions are excluded.

Phlebotomist produces interview answers and measured vital signs in retained s1, then records donor identity, date, measurement values and units, history source and unresolved questions within s2's nine retained hours. Missing or conflicting information is clarified manually, never replaced by an inferred eligibility flag.
Native record configuration is tested first. No new model, automatic acceptance or medical rule engine is introduced.
Two incremental phlebotomist hours per 100 baseline hours cover form freshness and access checks; clinical criteria remain existing professional governance.
unknowns: Authorised screening scope, donor record functions and current copying effort
research_questions: Does a checked information view reduce assembly time without reducing interview or clinical assessment?

already_counted.description: First record capture and screening-pack checks

incremental.description: Donor information forms and access upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94; gross6 less2 upkeep gives4 net. Already-organised screening records may save nothing and yield minus2; interview, measurements and assessment retain85.
